title: Surrounded Regions
statement: The board holds the characters X and O. An O region is captured when it is completely surrounded by X, meaning no cell of the region touches the border. Flip every captured region to X in place. The answer is the mutated board rather than a return value.
constraints: a region connects through the four side-adjacent neighbours, not diagonally
hints: Searching each O region and asking whether it reached the border works, but it re-walks regions and is fiddly to get right.
Invert the question. Rather than finding the surrounded regions, find the SURVIVORS: every O reachable from an O on the border.
Flood fill inward from the border Os, marking them temporarily. Then one sweep: marked cells become O, every other O becomes X. This is the same border-seeded idea as Pacific Atlantic Water Flow.

cases.name: interior region captured, border O survives
single O is on the border, so survives
a chain reaching the border saves the whole region
